run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: The log source named in the request cannot explain a P1 in the stated window: index app-261-prod-logs holds only 4 documents across the whole authorized 24h window (2026-11-20T05:49:21Z–2026-11-21T05:49:21Z), all level INFO, all timestamped between 2026-11-21T05:24:13Z and 05:49:13Z — roughly 5.5–6 hours after the alleged incident around 2026-11-20T23:49Z — and all saying checkout-service/payment-service are healthy (success rate 99.8%, p95 215ms and 220ms, 'All payment provider connections healthy'). The only workload logs retained for the incident hour contradict the premise: checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged only successful PlaceOrder → 'payment went through' → confirmation-email sequences from 23:30:56Z to 00:12:15Z with no error-level line (1392 previous-instance lines scanned by a regex filter for error/warn/fatal/failed/failure/500 returned no error), and payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Transaction complete.' with a transactionId after each 'Charge request received.' between 00:08:06Z and 00:29:54Z. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable on every attempt (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so checkout's own error-rate, 500 counts and latency in the window were not checked at all; the frontend container had no retained lines for the window. No namespace named app-261 exists on the cluster (only app-101 among app-* namespaces), so the writer of that index could not be inspected. I cannot name a root cause: the 500s are neither corroborated nor refuted by the available data, and the checkout container restart at 04:23:42Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, concurrent with control-plane pod restarts at 04:23:43Z) is outside the incident period and unexplained.

claims.text: Elasticsearch holds exactly one index, app-261-prod-logs, with 4 documents and 6.7kb store size; its mappings are cluster(keyword), level(keyword), message(text), service(keyword) and timestamp(date).

A 24h aggregation over app-261-prod-logs returned total 4 documents, all with level INFO, in a single hourly bucket 2026-11-21T05:00:00Z, from services checkout-service (3 documents) and payment-service (1 document); no document falls in any earlier hour, including the hour containing the alleged incident near 2026-11-20T23:49Z.

The four documents in app-261-prod-logs are: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 215ms' at 2026-11-21T05:49:13Z; checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes' at 05:44:13Z; payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 05:34:13Z; checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 05:24:13Z — all carrying cluster=production-eu-west-2.

checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged only successful order flows between 2026-11-20T23:30:56Z and 2026-11-21T00:12:15Z: repeating '[PlaceOrder] user_id=... user_currency=...', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent to ...' at severity info; no HTTP 500 or error line appears in that span.

A regex filter for error/warn/fatal/failed/failure/500 over checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logs 2026-11-20T23:00:00Z–2026-11-21T00:30:00Z read 1392 lines of the previous container instance and 404 of the current one, and returned no error-level line; its only two matches were info lines whose user_id text happens to contain the digits '500'.

payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged, between 2026-11-21T00:08:06Z and 00:29:54Z, 'Charge request received.' immediately followed by 'Transaction complete.' with a transactionId for each charge (USD and CAD amounts), i.e. payment charges were completing during the incident period.

The checkout and payment Services each resolve to exactly one ready endpoint: checkout → pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n at 10.244.0.12:8080 and payment → pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d at 10.244.0.17:8080, both port name tcp-service.
All 21 Deployments in namespace otel-demo, including checkout and payment, report readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1 at the time of the query (about 2026-11-21T05:49Z).

The fault-injection flag definitions in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) include paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad and recommendationCacheFailure, and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off' in the configuration readable now.

The checkout container in pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n has restartCount 1: its previous instance terminated with exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (started 2026-11-20T16:32:37Z) and the current instance started 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z — roughly 4.5 hours after the alleged incident window, concurrent with kube-system control-plane pods whose startTime is 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z.

The cluster's namespaces are app-101, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; there is no namespace named app-261, and namespace app-101 contains only pods loki-66445c6d6f-6sxbh and payment-api-101-8486559b69-xm8b2.

The only event returned for the authorized window was a Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for service app-282/loki — 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists' at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z — an object outside otel-demo and unrelated to checkout.

An earlier grouped event query over the same window counted 13 events, all in namespace app-100a: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet x2, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate x2, and Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started x2 each — a rollout in another tenant namespace, not of otel-demo checkout; namespace app-100a does not appear in the current namespace list.

If checkout did return 500s near 2026-11-20T23:49Z, no injected-fault mechanism can be confirmed or excluded for that period: the flagd flag definitions are only observable in their current state (all defaultVariant 'off') and change history is not integrated, so when paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable or another flag was last changed is unknown.

The absence of checkout error logs for the window may reflect missing telemetry rather than a healthy service: app-261-prod-logs has no document before 2026-11-21T05:24:13Z, and a short burst of 500s between the logged successful transactions would not necessarily appear in the retained lines.

Obtain the P1 alert's exact source, timestamp and query (alert name, service, cluster) before further action, because the index named in the request has no document in the incident window and the only retained workload logs show successful payments — the alert may refer to a different environment, cluster or service identity than otel-demo checkout in production-eu-west-2.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and then compare checkout's error spans and latency (for example status_code="ERROR" span counts, rpc_grpc_status_code and http_server_request_duration_seconds percentiles) over 2026-11-20T21:00Z–2026-11-21T02:00Z against a pre-incident baseline; no latency or error-rate trend can be asserted from the data gathered here.

gaps: The query of app-261-prod-logs restricted to 2026-11-20T22:00:00Z–2026-11-21T02:00:00Z returned no documents (status no_data, evidence id 08f77824-0efe-408d-9222-f23b954828a9-t0:10d39031-7883-4b21-bc88-8f56770676df), and the whole-window aggregation shows only 4 INFO documents in the 05:00 hour of 2026-11-21; that query's empty result shows only that it matched nothing, so whether checkout wrote other documents in the incident period is unknown.

Prometheus was unavailable on every attempt (get_label_values twice, execute_prometheus_instant_query twice, metrics_range_query twice, get_metric_names once, all SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so checkout error counts, status_code="ERROR" spans, rpc_grpc_status_code, app_payment_transactions_total and http_server_request_duration_seconds could not be read for the incident window; whether checkout returned 500s is unverified, not disproven.

Jaeger was unavailable on every attempt (traces_list_services and traces_search twice, all SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level evidence of checkout HTTP status codes, error spans, parent-child call edges or latency exists in this Run.

The frontend container of pod frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw had zero retained lines for 2026-11-20T23:30:00Z–2026-11-21T00:15:00Z (its previous instance contributed 0 lines; the read returned no_data, evidence id a70ae705-79ed-473d-ad78-195f31912fe9-t0:36dc4c54-e135-4e97-ad3b-d1b9a49c67e7), so customer-facing 500s could not be checked in frontend logs.

No namespace app-261 exists in the cluster, and the log documents carry service names checkout-service/payment-service that do not exist as Kubernetes workloads (the workloads are otel-demo/checkout and otel-demo/payment), so the producer of app-261-prod-logs could not be inspected; whether that index belongs to a deleted tenant namespace or a non-Kubernetes pipeline is unknown.

No events remain for namespace otel-demo (a grouped event query over otel-demo returned nothing, evidence id 4a2f278d-b2f6-4e3e-9caa-87c2a149249f-t1:07580bc2-e3b4-416d-906a-bb5ffaeb3ce6), so the cause of checkout's 04:23:42Z termination (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) and of the simultaneous 04:23:43Z control-plane pod restarts could not be determined.

A filtered read of checkout logs for 2026-11-21T03:50:00Z–04:30:00Z around the restart returned no matching line (status no_data, evidence id 4a2f278d-b2f6-4e3e-9caa-87c2a149249f-t0:3853103d-c6f4-4130-8478-28521b137f04), so the restart's trigger is unknown.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deploy, configuration edit, flag flip or infrastructure change can be correlated with 2026-11-20T23:49Z.

No latency baseline was available; the only latency figures are self-reported checkpoint lines (p95 215ms and 220ms) from 2026-11-21T05:24Z–05:49Z, outside the incident period, so no slowdown can be confirmed or excluded.

Kubernetes object reads reflect cluster state at query time (about 2026-11-21T05:49Z), not the state during the incident window, so replica counts, endpoints and restart counters observed now cannot prove the workload's state around 23:49Z.
next_steps: Confirm with the alerting system which cluster, service and time the P1 refers to; the data here is tagged production-eu-west-2 but the named index has no incident-window documents.

Once Prometheus/Jaeger access is restored, query checkout error rate and p95 latency over 2026-11-20T21:00Z–2026-11-21T02:00Z against a pre-incident baseline and inspect checkout spans with error status tags.
Review the change-history system (not integrated here) for deploys, ConfigMap edits and flagd flag changes near 2026-11-20T23:49Z and near the 04:23Z cluster restart.
Check whether log shipping into app-261-prod-logs has stopped or retention is truncated: 4 documents in 24 hours for a serving production service is a telemetry gap, not evidence of health.
Investigate why the checkout container and the cluster control plane restarted at 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z, for example node or host maintenance on opspilot-m1-control-plane.
